title: Testing Assumptions, Not Ideas
editorial_note: Opening revised to lead with the lesson itself. Remaining dialogue is an automated editorial draft; review spoken wording and meaning before final publication.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Testing Assumptions, Not Ideas.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Ideas are bundles of assumptions. Test the assumption with the highest risk first: that people want the outcome, can understand the solution, will use it in context, that it can be delivered, or that it will create value without unacceptable harm. This makes learning faster and protects teams from polishing an unproven premise.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Why does that happen?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Write a testable hypothesis with a predicted behaviour and a threshold for changing direction. Match fidelity to the question: a sketch can test comprehension; a concierge service can test demand; a technical spike can test feasibility. Do not build a full product merely to learn a narrow fact.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: Test the weakest link with the smallest honest representation
turns.text: What changes when we look at test the weakest link with the smallest honest representation?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Tests match the claim. A data audit tests coverage and freshness; a comprehension prototype tests interpretation; a concierge workflow tests ownership; a limited pilot tests behaviour under real conditions. Each test defines expected evidence, threshold, limitation, and resulting decision before it runs. A positive reaction cannot compensate for a failed safety assumption.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: Worked contrast: a successful test can answer the wrong question
turns.text: What changes when we look at worked contrast: a successful test can answer the wrong question?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Six participants correctly use a polished clinic-comparison prototype. The team concludes that comparison is validated. In reality, the prototype contained accurate hand-authored options, while the production risk is whether supplier data can identify clinically equivalent, current availability. The usability assumption gained support; feasibility and safety remain untested.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at decompose the bet?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: List assumptions across desirability, usability, viability, feasibility, accessibility, ethics, data, operations, and adoption. Phrase each so evidence could prove it weaker: “Target customers can recognise an acceptable substitute before checkout,” not “people like substitutions.”

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Rate uncertainty and consequence if false. Test the riskiest assumption with the smallest method that can change the decision: interview or observation, fake door, prototype, concierge, technical spike, policy review, or controlled rollout. One test rarely validates the whole idea.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Define evidence and decision thresholds in advance. Record result, limits, and next action. Positive reactions do not prove behaviour; successful use does not prove value; technical feasibility does not prove responsible deployment. Assumption testing keeps these confidence layers separate.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: Design the smallest test that can change the decision
turns.text: What changes when we look at design the smallest test that can change the decision?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: The test plan states predicted evidence and possible actions before results arrive. Positive reaction cannot compensate for failed safety or feasibility. A fake door may estimate interest but cannot promise a care route that does not exist. Manual delivery can reveal value but not prove automation or scale.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Results update the assumption register and next decision, including stop or narrow. The team values invalidated ideas because they prevent expensive commitment; it does not redesign the metric until the idea appears successful.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Where does the harder design decision appear?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: The riskiest assumption is often organisationally inconvenient rather than technically difficult. Name it anyway; otherwise a team can build certainty around the least important question.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What should we look at more closely?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Decompose an idea before testing it. A proposed “smart reminder” may assume the event can be predicted, people want a reminder, the timing is acceptable, the message is understandable, the delivery channel is trusted, and the reminder changes behaviour without causing stress or unwanted disclosure. Different assumptions need different evidence.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Testing the polish of the message cannot validate demand or feasibility.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Choose the least expensive representation that can answer the riskiest question. A story, interview, or observed workaround may test problem relevance; a sketch may test comprehension; a concierge or Wizard-of-Oz service may test whether people value a result; a technical prototype may test feasibility; a limited rollout may test real behaviour and unintended effects.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Define a decision rule before the study to reduce the temptation to reinterpret ambiguous results as approval.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Failure modes to watch

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Idea voting: preference for a polished concept substitutes for evidence. Wrong-fidelity test: a high-fidelity prototype is used to answer a simple demand question. Success without threshold: any positive comment is taken as a go signal. Ignored downside: a test observes benefit but not privacy, accessibility, support, or trust costs.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Can we see that in a concrete product situation?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: A fake-door test can estimate interest in same-day delivery but should not promise a consequential service without explaining availability. It cannot prove operational feasibility or willingness to pay.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: How does this connect to what we have already learned?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Opportunity mapping identifies possible directions. Assumption testing decides what evidence is needed before investing. lesson 30 makes that learning visible to the people who must trust it.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What should I notice the next time I use a product?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Pick one solution and state its riskiest desirability, viability, feasibility, or usability assumption.
